text.tspan: AWS Transfer Family vs AWS DataSync
• Into and out of S3 or EFS, access via an IAM role
• Protocols: SFTP, FTPS, FTP, AS2 (+ browser web apps)
• FTP is clear text: VPC (internal) endpoint only
• Pay per provisioned endpoint per hour + per GB
• Users: stored in the service, or your existing
auth (Microsoft AD, LDAP, Okta, Cognito, custom)
• Optional Route 53 name for the endpoint
• Use: sharing files, public datasets, CRM, ERP
• Agent → AWS over TLS (encrypted in transit)
• Needs an agent: on-prem storage, or EFS/FSx ↔ other clouds
• No agent: AWS ↔ AWS (same or other account,
any Region), S3 ↔ other clouds' object storage
• Per task: 10 Gbps with agent, 5 Gbps without;
• External partners PUSH or PULL files with an FTP/SFTP client → Transfer Family.
• Copy or keep in sync large data sets on a schedule (migration, replication between AWS storage services) → DataSync.
• Apps on-prem must keep using files / volumes / tapes with a local cache → Storage Gateway.
• Too much data for the network (more than a week) → Snowball (existing customers) or Data Transfer Terminal / partner devices.
• Hybrid pattern: DataSync for the initial migration, then Storage Gateway (S3 File Gateway) for ongoing on-prem access.
